feature_name: Cloud Bigtable monitoring in GCP Console
summary: The GCP Console added improved Cloud Bigtable monitoring with new charts for cluster storage utilization, node count, and replication status.
extended_definition: The GCP Console added improved Cloud Bigtable monitoring with new charts for cluster storage utilization, node count, and replication status.

supporting_pages.title: Bigtable for Cassandra users \_|\_ Google Cloud Documentation
evidence_snippets: The Bigtable Google Cloud console page comes with prebuilt dashboards for tracking throughput and utilization metrics at the instance, cluster, and table levels.
The Bigtable Key Visualizer , a monitoring feature in the Google Cloud console, lets you perform advanced performance tuning.
You can change the cluster size manually in the Google Cloud console or programmatically using the Cloud Bigtable API.

supporting_pages.title: Autoscaling \_|\_ Bigtable \_|\_ Google Cloud Documentation
evidence_snippets: You can also view these metrics using Cloud Monitoring . bigtable.googleapis.com/cluster/autoscaling/min node count bigtable.googleapis.com/cluster/autoscaling/max node count bigtable.googleapis.com/cluster/autoscaling/recommended node count for cpu bigtable.googleapis.com/cluster/autoscaling/recommended node count for storage Logging Bigtable emits a system event audit log each time it scales a cluster.
When a node is added to a small cluster, such as a one-node cluster, you might observe a temporary increase in latency as the cluster rebalances.
You can view autoscaling system event logs on the Bigtable cluster overview page in the Google Cloud console.
